analogs.covers: Body and glide: a palm-sized climber that sails from tree to tree across long gaps instead of touching the ground, sleeps high up and rests together with its colony
Voice and temper: a brilliant mimic with a long memory for faces that swoops screeching at anything near its nest tree and lives in noisy, bickering groups

headline: A sugar glider with a magpie's voice: the far-gliding Microraptor of the heights, cliffs and open water that sails across gaps the others cannot, copies every call and dive-bombs anything near its nest tree.

setting.label: Heights, wind canyons and open water to glide across
setting.note: Zhaoianus hatch in Big Tree Overlook, Wind Tunnels, Cliff Edge Falls, Black Fern Hills, Volcano Islands and Stillwater Bog: lookouts, wind, cliffs and wide water to cross. Big Tree Overlook is also every subspecies' courtship ground. Border land: Crag Bluffs, Coastal Bluffs, the tall Redwoods and Steep Run. Everything else is roaming ground. Never in caves.

playsLike: You are a Zhaoianus, the gliding subspecies: you hatched on the heights, in the wind canyons or by wide water and can glide for longer. You are the smallest carnivore on the roster (Tiny, 500 combat weight, 400 HP, a 40 bite that only hurts targets under 600 combat weight, land sprint 825 for 400 s). You climb trunks and cliffs, glide from tree to tree and sleep in short bursts high up, never in caves. You live on carrion, insects and critters and hunt only Juvenile-and-younger Deinonychus, Latenivenatrix, Psittacosaurus and Struthiomimus, even guarded ones, plus Rhamphorhynchus, with at most one partner. Your weapon is mimicry: copied calls lure the parents away from their nest. In a scurry of up to 10 you swarm and dive-bomb anything that hunts you, except Apex carnivores and the six species you always flee from; as a pair or alone you may claim an Apex carnivore as your companion, ride on its side and learn its calls.

why.text: Zhaoianus “are able to glide for longer”. Sugar gliders sail up to about 50 metres from one tree to the next instead of climbing down (official inspiration: sugar gliders).

Zhaoianus hatch at the Volcano Islands and Stillwater Bog, where the next landing lies across open water. Even they complain: “Crossing large bodies of water may cause them extra distress”, they just make it across more easily.
In a scurry “all Microraptor take time to rest in unison”, like a sugar glider colony asleep in one hollow.

Microraptor “are most commonly known for their mimicry of other species” and parrot calls back at tolerant species in “conversations”. Australian magpies are among the best vocal mimics, copying other birds, dogs and even sirens.

They “have an excellent memory, often recalling not only calls they’ve heard, but past experiences they have had with certain species”. Australian magpies recognise individual people for years and swoop only at the ones they remember as a threat.

Any intruder on a claimed nest tree is “met immediately with loud, screeching protests, with members swooping overhead repeatedly”: the magpie's swooping season, with small pecks included (official inspiration: magpies).

notLike: Australian magpies walk and fly; Microraptor climbs, glides and only hops about on the ground.
Magpie groups defend a large territory all year; Microraptor claims only its nest tree, a cliff ledge or its carnivore companion, and flees at the first sign of aggression.
Sugar gliders are nocturnal and live on sap and nectar; Microraptor is cathemeral and lives on carrion, insects and critters.
twist: The subspecies of open air: where a Gui climbs and a Hanqiugi endures, a Zhaoianus simply glides on.
